program.merge_policy: accumulate twenty 25-entry deep passes; consolidate and validate once after Wave 2500

source_provenance: Public PubMed/PMC abstracts and ordinary web research
manual clinical-identity, route, formulation, population, evidence-quality and safety calibration

policy.validation_strategy: deep source calibration per pass; expensive repository-wide validation after Wave 2500

rejected_candidates.title: Efficacy, Durability, and Safety of Collagen Biostimulators Based on Poly-L-Lactic Acid (PLLA) and Calcium Hydroxyapatite (CaHA) in the Face: A Systematic Review.
rejected_candidates.reason: injectable aesthetic biomaterials; title-level collagen identity is not collagen supplement evidence

rejected_candidates.title: Starch aerogels as nutraceutical carriers: Experimental and computational strategies for designing a delivery system.
rejected_candidates.reason: materials/delivery-system engineering, not human supplement efficacy or safety evidence

waves.title: Efficacy of melatonin vs. midazolam for oral premedication in children: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
waves.population: 774 children aged 1-15 undergoing anesthesia
waves.finding: Oral melatonin and midazolam did not differ significantly for sedation or perioperative anxiety outcomes in pooled comparisons.
waves.safety: This is pediatric premedication evidence in an anesthesia setting and should not be generalized to routine sleep supplementation.

waves.title: The effect of saffron supplementation on liver and kidney function, blood glucose and pressure in patients with diabetes and prediabetes: A grade assessed systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
waves.population: people with diabetes or prediabetes
waves.finding: Saffron/crocin modestly reduced systolic blood pressure, fasting glucose, and AST, but did not significantly improve diastolic pressure, ALT, or kidney-function markers; the authors judged observed effects clinically unimportant.
waves.safety: Statistical significance should not be confused with clinically meaningful benefit.

waves.title: Effects of Synbiotic Supplementation on Blood and Urinary Concentrations of Factors Related to Kidney Stone Formation in Overweight or Obese Patients with Hyperoxaluria: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
waves.population: 44 overweight or obese adults with hyperoxaluria
waves.finding: Twelve weeks of synbiotic supplementation reduced urinary oxalate versus placebo but did not significantly alter other measured blood or urine stone-risk factors.
waves.safety: Small single trial measured biochemical risk factors rather than confirmed stone recurrence.

waves.title: Research Review: Omega-3 supplementation to reduce antisocial behavior - a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
waves.population: 2,889 participants across child and adult behavioral studies
waves.finding: Omega-3 supplementation produced a statistically significant but small reduction in antisocial behavior; stratified effects were not clearly explained by age, sex, dose, sample size, or study quality.
waves.safety: Effect magnitude was small and publication-bias evidence was equivocal; behavioral outcomes span heterogeneous populations.

waves.title: Ginkgo biloba extract EGb 761 is safe and effective in the treatment of mild dementia - a meta-analysis of patient subgroups in randomised controlled trials.
waves.population: 782 patients with mild dementia
waves.finding: The standardized EGb 761 extract improved cognition, global assessment, activities of daily living, and quality of life versus placebo, with similar adverse-event frequency.
waves.safety: Evidence is specific to the standardized EGb 761 pharmaceutical extract and cannot be generalized to generic Ginkgo products.

waves.title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of the acute effect of caffeine on attention.
waves.study: meta-analysis of 31 randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trials
waves.population: 1,455 rested healthy adults
waves.finding: Acute caffeine modestly improved attention accuracy and reaction time; higher doses improved reaction time further while accuracy showed a nonlinear relationship.
waves.safety: Dose-response findings do not establish a universally optimal dose and higher acute doses can carry individual tolerability risks.

waves.title: Effects of Probiotic and Synbiotic Supplementation on Body Composition and Glucose Metabolism in Children and Adolescents with Overweight or Obesity: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
waves.population: children and adolescents with overweight or obesity
waves.finding: Probiotic/synbiotic supplementation produced only a small, low-certainty BMI reduction and did not clearly improve BMI-z, waist circumference, body fat, fasting glucose, insulin, or HOMA-IR.
waves.safety: Pediatric, strain-specific evidence is low certainty and does not support broad metabolic claims.

waves.title: Beneficial Impacts of pre- and Postoperative Probiotics/Synbiotics Supplementation in Patients Undergoing Gastrointestinal Surgeries: An Umbrella Meta-Analysis.
waves.population: patients undergoing gastrointestinal surgery
waves.finding: Perioperative probiotic/synbiotic use was associated with fewer postoperative infections and diarrhea, shorter hospital stay, lower mortality, and reduced antibiotic duration.
waves.safety: This is adjunctive perioperative clinical-care evidence across heterogeneous formulations and surgeries, not routine wellness supplementation.

waves.title: Probiotic Lactobacillus sp. as a strategy for modulation of non-comorbid obesity: A systematic meta-analysis and GRADE assessment of randomized controlled trials.
waves.population: 1,058 people with obesity without major comorbidities
waves.finding: Lactobacillus-based probiotics produced small reductions in BMI, body weight, waist and hip circumference, and several fat measures, with changes in leptin and adiponectin and no significant adverse-event signal.
waves.safety: Effects are strain-specific and modest; Lactobacillus is not a single interchangeable intervention.

waves.title: Effects of Probiotic Supplementation on Mental Health and the Risk of Depression in Women with Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials.
waves.population: adult women with PCOS
waves.finding: Probiotic/synbiotic interventions were associated with improvements in some sleep, depressive-symptom, and quality-of-life measures, but the evidence base was small and methodologically variable.
waves.safety: Small study count and mixed probiotic/synbiotic/enriched-food interventions preclude broad mental-health claims.

waves.title: Therapeutic potential of curcumin in colorectal cancer - A systematic review.
waves.population: mixed mechanistic and limited translational colorectal-cancer evidence
waves.finding: Curcumin shows pro-apoptotic, anti-inflammatory, cell-cycle, and chemotherapy-sensitization mechanisms, with nanoformulations proposed to improve bioavailability.
waves.safety: The review explicitly notes that clinical trials are still needed to validate efficacy and safety; it cannot support a cancer-treatment claim.

waves.title: Unraveling Riboflavin-Mediated Mitochondrial Modulation as a Therapeutic Pathway in Neurological Disorders: An Integrative Systematic Review.
waves.population: 6 in-vitro studies, 10 rodent studies, and 7 clinical trials across neurological conditions
waves.finding: Riboflavin has plausible mitochondrial and redox mechanisms and some human signals in selected neurological settings, but most condition-specific evidence remains mechanistic or preclinical.
waves.safety: Human applications are insufficiently defined for most diseases; established migraine contexts should be kept separate from speculative neurodegeneration claims.

waves.title: Autophagy activation in granulosa cells as a mechanism of astaxanthin action: evidence from a pilot randomised trial in PMOS-associated infertility.
waves.population: 44 completers with PCOS/PMOS-related anovulatory infertility
waves.finding: Astaxanthin altered granulosa-cell autophagy/apoptosis signaling and increased adjusted total and mature-oocyte yields and embryo-quality measures, while pregnancy outcomes were numerically but not significantly higher.
waves.safety: Small exploratory fertility trial with surrogate laboratory/embryology outcomes; pregnancy and live-birth benefit is unproven.

waves.title: Effects of vitamin D supplementation on patients with systemic lupus erythematosus: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
waves.population: 847 people with systemic lupus erythematosus
waves.finding: Vitamin D supplementation increased 25(OH)D and modestly reduced pooled SLE disease activity and improved complement markers, while ESR, fatigue severity, and anti-dsDNA levels were not clearly improved.
waves.safety: Disease-specific adjunctive evidence is mixed and should not be generalized beyond SLE.

waves.title: Best Evidence Summary of Folic Acid Supplementation for Prevention of Neural Tube Defects in Women of Childbearing Age.
waves.population: women of childbearing age and preconception/pregnancy populations
waves.finding: High-level guidance consistently supports preconception folic-acid supplementation for neural-tube-defect prevention, with higher doses reserved for clinically defined higher-risk groups.
waves.safety: This is guideline synthesis rather than a new efficacy trial; high-risk dosing belongs under clinical guidance rather than consumer dose extrapolation.

waves.title: Effect of Probiotic Supplementation on Cariogenic Streptococcus mutans Levels: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
waves.population: human participants with quantitative Streptococcus mutans outcomes
waves.finding: Probiotic interventions produced limited, transient, strain-dependent reductions in S. mutans and did not show a consistent statistically significant advantage over placebo across intervals.
waves.safety: Evidence supports, at most, an adjunctive experimental role and not replacement of established caries prevention.

waves.title: Molecular mechanisms and therapeutic potential of quercetin in ovarian functions.
waves.population: mixed human and predominantly experimental ovarian literature
waves.finding: Quercetin affects oxidative stress, inflammation, apoptosis, mitochondrial pathways, and steroidogenesis in ovarian disease models, but robust clinical efficacy evidence is sparse.
waves.safety: Mechanistic and animal evidence dominates; long-term human efficacy, dose, and safety remain uncertain.

waves.title: Ginseng Berry Concentrate Alleviates Fatigue in Humans: A Randomized, Placebo-Controlled, Double-Blinded Clinical Trial.
waves.population: 88 adults with substantial daily fatigue
waves.finding: A proprietary ginseng-berry concentrate improved selected fatigue questionnaire outcomes and reduced resting lactate versus placebo; broader questionnaire benefits were stronger in an exploratory medication-exclusion subgroup.
waves.safety: Small, product-specific study with subgroup dependence; results cannot be generalized to all ginseng preparations.

waves.title: Influence of melatonin supplementation on cancer-related fatigue: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
waves.population: people with cancer-related fatigue
waves.finding: Melatonin produced a small pooled reduction in cancer-related fatigue, with benefit concentrated in longer-duration studies.
waves.safety: Cancer population and treatment context limit generalization; duration meta-regression is exploratory rather than dosing guidance.

waves.title: Effects of Saffron Supplementation on Glycolipid Metabolism and Blood Pressure in Patients With Metabolic Syndrome and Related Disorders: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
waves.population: 1,486 participants with metabolic syndrome or related disorders
waves.finding: Saffron modestly reduced fasting glucose, HbA1c, total cholesterol, and systolic/diastolic pressure, while HOMA-IR, triglycerides, LDL-C, HDL-C, BMI, and waist circumference were not significantly improved.
waves.safety: Effect sizes were generally small and condition-specific; larger diverse trials are needed.

waves.title: Collagen-ORC Versus Standard Treatment in Diabetic Foot Ulcers: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomised Trials.
waves.population: 314 adults with diabetic foot ulcers across six studies
waves.finding: Collagen-combination dressings increased complete wound closure in a small focused meta-analysis, but trials were small, heterogeneous, and frequently single-center.
waves.safety: This is topical wound-dressing evidence, not evidence for oral collagen supplementation.

waves.title: Effect of omega-3 supplementation vs. placebo on blood lipid levels in patients with ischemic heart disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
waves.population: 633 adults with ischemic heart disease
waves.finding: Omega-3 supplementation lowered triglycerides and LDL-C versus placebo, with moderate-certainty evidence for those lipid outcomes and smaller/less stable effects on other lipids.
waves.safety: Secondary-prevention patients and doses/formulations varied; lipid changes do not by themselves establish cardiovascular-event benefit.

waves.title: Cognitive Benefits of Ginseng: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Changes in Mini-Mental State Examination and Alzheimer's Disease Assessment Scale-Cognitive Subscale Scores.
waves.population: people with subjective memory impairment, MCI, or Alzheimer's disease
waves.finding: Ginseng produced small improvements in pooled MMSE and ADAS-Cog scores, but heterogeneity and limited trial numbers leave long-term clinical relevance uncertain.
waves.safety: Different ginseng products and doses were pooled; formulation-specific evidence should not be treated as interchangeable.

waves.title: Effects of Caffeine Supplementation on Exercise Performance in Volleyball Players: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
waves.study: systematic review/meta-analysis of 11 blinded crossover studies
waves.population: volleyball players
waves.finding: Caffeine improved attack/serve accuracy, jump performance, handgrip strength, agility time, and positive simulated-game actions in pooled analyses.
waves.safety: Sport-specific acute performance evidence does not define an optimal or universally safe caffeine dose.

waves.title: Association Between Dietary Calcium or Dairy Product Intake and Metabolic Syndrome Risk: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
waves.population: adults assessed for dietary calcium/dairy intake and metabolic syndrome
waves.finding: Higher dietary calcium and dairy intake were associated with lower metabolic-syndrome prevalence and more favorable component profiles.
waves.safety: Cross-sectional food-intake associations cannot establish causality or support calcium-supplement treatment claims.
